newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won ends nearly flat, no impact from strikes.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won ends nearly flat, no impact from strikes.

text.p: The South Korean won ended Friday's trading nearly flat as players remained cautious in the face of the central bank's committment to support the domestic unit, traders said.
The won closed at 843.60, up slightly from the opening of 843.70. It ranged from 843.20 to 844.10.
"The Bank of Korea's determinatin to keep the U.S. currency capped at 845 has moved some banks to carry short dollar positions," said a local bank dealer.
Strikes at major export industries such as shipping and automaking have not had a major impact on the forex markets, traders said.
The strikes are in protest at a labour bill which was railroaded through parliament on Thursday.
"There's no effect yet, but if the strikes continue into mid-January, especially in sectors like automaking, the problem could spread into the market," the local trader said.
The won/dollar rate was seen moving in a tight 843-845 range on Monday.
